# Decisions

This file records durable engineering and presentation choices for ssmithnet.net.

## ADR-001 — Static output, compiled generator

**Decision.** The deployed site is ordinary static HTML/assets generated by a first-party C++ program.

**Rationale.** Runtime simplicity, reproducibility and long-term inspectability are more valuable here than a server-side or JavaScript application framework.

**Consequence.** Site structure and repeated composition belong in `src/sitegen.cpp`; generated HTML mirrors are not edited by hand.

## ADR-002 — Generated review mirrors remain byte-verifiable

**Decision.** Generated HTML is committed for review but must match generator output exactly.

**Rationale.** Reviewers can inspect the result without creating a second editable source of truth.

**Consequence.** Validation regenerates the pages and rejects drift.

## ADR-003 — Shared web primitives come from Common, identity stays local

**Decision.** Generic escaping, durable publication, design tokens and deploy mechanics may come from pinned Common; content, information architecture and personal visual identity remain in this repository.

**Rationale.** Shared infrastructure should not flatten the site's identity or create private duplicate helpers.

**Consequence.** Common changes are pinned/reviewed and site-specific styling remains local.

## ADR-004 — The visual language is materially rich but restrained

**Decision.** The site uses the established dark blue-black, graphite/silver, cool cyan and restrained warm-material language rather than generic SaaS/minimalist conventions.

**Rationale.** The site is intended to feel personal, engineered and long-lived rather than template-driven.

**Consequence.** New sections reuse the existing design grammar instead of inventing new card/badge systems.

## ADR-005 — Information belongs in one authoritative section

**Decision.** Home teases; Workbench owns technical projects; Garage owns vehicle history; Archive owns historical site material.

**Rationale.** Repeating the same detailed content across pages makes maintenance harder and weakens information hierarchy.

**Consequence.** New content is placed according to subject ownership rather than duplicated for visibility.

## ADR-006 — One website family, two product surfaces

**Decision.** The personal site owns the canonical website shell and assets. Package Repository consumes a pinned, byte-verified snapshot.

**Rationale.** Both sites belong to Shannon Smith and must retain one identity without depending on a runtime request to the other host. Common's neutral primitives remain shared across the wider application family.

**Consequence.** A shared identity change updates both consumers; deployment checks prevent independently edited snapshots. The download page also uses the canonical shell.
